criteria.criterion: The diff touches only crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs, contains no change to existing test code, and the extracted code moves without changed logic.
criteria.evidence: The diff changes planning.rs and CHANGELOG.md. CHANGELOG.md is on the expected deliverables list, which is the one statement of scope, so it is not a scope violation. The diff contains no test code. On logic: I compared the moved code line by line. `round` now comes from `plan.round`, and plan_record sets that field from the `round` argument (line 569), so the value is the same. `last_round`, `cfg`, `id`, `p`, `request`, `grant`, `snap_dir` and `no_env` are recomputed in critic_round from the same `ctx` inputs and give the same values, including the same `plan-{round}` snapshot directory. The mechanical-stop message, reason, Critique fields and the order of pushes and stop_planning are unchanged; `max_rounds` comes from the same config. The early-return paths still return `RoundEnd::Stopped`.

findings.summary: critic_round repeats the setup that planning_round already does (cfg, id, p, request, grant, snap_dir, no_env) instead of receiving these values from the caller.
findings.evidence: The same expressions appear at lines 94-109 and again at lines 306-322. The values are identical, so behavior does not change, but the setup is now written twice. A small struct for the shared round context would remove the duplication. This is taste, not a correctness problem.

summary: The change passes. It splits the 291-line planning_round into planning_round (171 lines), a new stop_on_mechanical_limit (41 lines) and a new critic_round (134 lines), all private and in the same file, plus a CHANGELOG entry. No function in planning.rs is now longer than 200 lines. I compared the moved code with the base. It behaves the same: `round` is taken from `plan.round`, which plan_record sets from the same argument, and the other recomputed values come from the same inputs. The checks Athena recorded (fmt, clippy, test) passed. My own run of the 138 athena-core tests matching 'plan' also passed, including the test of the mechanical-limit stop and the critic tests. The diff touches only the two expected deliverables and no test code. The one finding is a nit: critic_round repeats the setup lines that planning_round already runs.
